records.confirmation_evidence: Research Ireland's live programme page for the Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme states it is 'Closed' for the 2026 call, with an applicant deadline of '23rd October 2025, 16:00 Irish local time', a duration of '1-4 years', and a value of 'up to a maximum of €34,000 per annum in any approved year'.

new_scholarship.name: Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme
legacy_titles: Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme 2027
new_scholarship.description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme provides individual, prestigious awards for excellent research in the name of the applicant at an eligible higher education institution in Ireland. It funds all disciplines from archaeology to zoology and supports bottom-up, non-directed research, except for awards funded by strategic funding partners. Research Ireland reports an average success rate of 18% over the past five years. The 2026 call closed on 23 October 2025 with a stated value of up to EUR 34,000 per annum.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: 2026 call (closed); next cycle expected September 2027 following the annual cycle
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The page lists the 2026 applicant deadline as 23rd October 2025, 16:00 Irish local time, alongside an FAQ deadline of 16th October 2025, a supervisor/mentor deadline of 6th November 2025 and a research office endorsement deadline of 13th November 2025, all shown as achieved. The programme runs on an annual call cycle but no 2027 date has been published, so the deadline_date is null.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The Research Ireland page shows the 2026 call as 'Closed' with call outcome at end of April 2026 and an award start date of 1st September 2026. The programme operates as an annual national initiative, so the next call is expected to open around September 2027, but no 2027 date has been published.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The page states the award consists of a stipend of EUR 25,000 per annum, 'a contribution to fees, including non-EU fees, up to a maximum of EUR 5,750 per annum', and 'eligible direct costs of EUR 3,250 per annum'. Non-EU recipients may request an additional EUR 4,000 per annum over and above the standard fee contribution, with any remaining differential paid by the recipient and/or the research body.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Up to EUR 34,000 per annum: EUR 25,000 stipend, up to EUR 5,750 fee contribution (plus EUR 4,000 for non-EU), and EUR 3,250 eligible direct costs
benefits: Fee contribution including non-EU fees up to EUR 5,750 per annum
Eligible direct research costs of EUR 3,250 per annum
Individual awards for excellent research in the name of the applicant
eligibility: New entrants to a Master's or PhD programme, or registered students in the first year of the degree for which funding is sought (effective from the 2026 call)
Applicants at an eligible higher education institution in Ireland
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants of all nationalities applying through an eligible Irish research body
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to all nationalities, including non-EU applicants, who are hosted at an eligible Irish higher education institution
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time research degree at an eligible higher education institution in Ireland
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: Applicants propose their own bottom-up, non-directed research project; pioneering proposals addressing new and emerging fields and interdisciplinary proposals are encouraged
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Funding across all disciplines, from archaeology to zoology; awards for bottom-up, non-directed research, with the exception of those funded by strategic funding partners
programme_detail_official.application_method: Online application through the Research Ireland grants management system, submitted by the applicant, with supervisor, mentor and research office endorsement forms submitted separately
requirements: Research office endorsement of the host institution
programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: The programme page does not state an English language test requirement; applicants should confirm requirements with the host research body.
selection_criteria: Excellent research potential, assessed by international, independent expert peer review
Objective selection process using international peer review
programme_detail_official.selection_weighting: Selection is by international, independent expert peer review; the page notes an average success rate of 18% over the past five years
award_holder_conditions: Award is held for the research project named in the application
Awardees are recognised as demonstrating world-class potential as future research leaders
supplements_or_initiatives: Strategic funding partners for 2026: Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Children Equality Disability Integration and Youth, Department of Foreign Affairs, and Met Eireann
programme_detail_official.description: An established national initiative funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science and managed by Research Ireland, offering individual awards for bottom-up, non-directed research across all disciplines.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Individual postgraduate research award supporting bottom-up, non-directed research
programme_detail_official.coverage: Stipend, fees contribution and eligible direct research costs

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are either a new entrant to a Master's or PhD programme or a registered first-year student (2026 call rule)
Identify a supervisor who can act as primary supervisor for no more than one applicant
Prepare the indicative application form and the research proposal for a bottom-up, non-directed project
Plan for the FAQ deadline of 16th October, which falls before the applicant deadline
Allow the research office time to endorse before the endorsement deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying as a continuing student beyond the first year of the degree
Submitting after the intermediate supervisor or research office deadlines have passed
Proposing directed research that belongs to a strategic funding partner strand
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any fee differential beyond the fee contribution for non-EU recipients
Costs not classed as eligible direct costs

alerts.message: The 2026 call closed on 23rd October 2025. The programme runs annually, so monitor Research Ireland for the next call opening.

submission_workflow: Applicant completes the online application before the applicant deadline
Supervisor and mentor submit their forms by their deadline
International expert peer review assesses the application
Call outcome announced at end of April
